content: The test image shows a tomato stem with dense gray-white fuzzy/powdery fungal growth, with dead/wilted brown leaves nearby. Now let me read the part index.

The Gray_Mold leaf shows brown lesions but not the dense spore mass. Let me check Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers.

Phytophthora shows dark brown/black wilting stems, no gray growth. Let me check the other Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot stem to see white mycelium.

I've used all 8 reference image views. Now making my final assessment.

**Test image analysis:**
- Stem affected: dense gray-white fuzzy/powdery growth covering the stem at a branch junction
- Leaves above are dead and brown (wilted/collapsed)
- Location: mid-plant (not at soil line)
- Gray fluffy coating = fungal spore mass

**Comparison summary:**
- Gray_Mold stem reference (Bugwood_14): showed a brown lesion without visible spore mass (dry conditions), but description says "dense velvety gray-brown spore mass" girdling stem causing wilting above — fits the test image pattern
- Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot: bleached stem with embedded black sclerotia — no match
- Southern_Blight: dry rot cross-section — no match
- Alternaria: dark black canker at soil line — no match
- Phytophthora: dark brown/black collapse — no match

The gray-white dense fuzzy coating on the stem + dead wilted leaves above = Gray Mold (Botrytis cinerea). The girdling of the stem by the spore mass causing collapse above is the defining feature.
